dialog.body: City Clerk's office, this is Owen. How can I help you?
Hi, yeah, good morning. Vincent Ricci. I'm calling about a dog. Well, a lost dog, a poster for a lost dog, and I want to know if I can register it with you or whoever does that.
Okay. A lost dog poster. Let me make sure I have this right. You found a poster, or you put one up?

Put one up. Well, my neighbor did, but she asked me to call because she's at work and she can't pick up during the day. So it's her dog, a beagle mix, brown and white, about, I want to say forty pounds. He's got a green collar. Which, funny thing, she bought that collar at a place out on Aquidneck, no, it was the one near the, never mind, that's not the point.
That's all right. Take your time. Before we go on, I want to say I'm having a little trouble hearing you. There's an echo on the line.
Yeah, sorry, I'm on speakerphone. I'm in the bathroom. It echoes in here, I know, but it's the only room in the house where I get any reception. Everywhere else it drops. The kitchen, forget it.
Understood. Go ahead, I can make it out. Just a bit slower if you can.

Sure, sure. So the dog's name is Biscuit. He got out Sunday night, I think around eight, when she opened the front door for a delivery. And she's been walking around calling him since. She put up posters on the poles and at the corner store. And somebody told her there's a way to register it with the city so if somebody finds him they know who to call.
Right. Let me ask, was Biscuit licensed with the city, do you know? Does he have a tag on the collar?
A tag, I think so. I think there's a rabies tag. I don't know about a license. I could ask her. She'd know. Actually, she told me one time the vet did the paperwork, so maybe.
Okay. That's fine. For a lost dog report, I can take down the details and pass them along to the right people. Do you want me to do that?
Yes, please. That's what I'm after. And, um, can I ask who actually responds? Like if somebody sees him, who do they call, who goes out? Is it the police or is it a separate animal control person?

In Newport, animal control officers handle stray and lost dogs. They work under the police department. So if someone spots him, they can call that line and an officer can respond. I'll get this report to them so they know to watch for him.

Okay, good. That makes sense. Because last year, and this is a different story, there was a dog on our street, a big black lab, hanging around for like three days, and nobody knew who to call. People were calling the fire department. It was a whole thing. One guy gave it a hot dog. Anyway.
Well, hopefully this time it's quicker. Let me get the details. What's the address where Biscuit lives, or where he got out?
It's 313 Callender Avenue. That's in the North End. Her house, I'm next door. Same street.
Three thirteen Callender Avenue. Got it. And the owner's name, is that something you can give me?
Um, I'd rather she give that herself, honestly. I can give you my name and number as the contact. Vincent Ricci. R-I-C-C-I. And the number is 401-555-0161.
Vincent Ricci, R-I-C-C-I, four oh one, five five five, zero one six one. Is that right?
That's it. Yeah. The reception in the bathroom is good enough for calls, just not for talking to people in the other room.

[pause] Okay. Now the description. Brown and white beagle mix, about forty pounds, green collar, named Biscuit. Missing since Sunday evening, around eight. Anything else? Any markings, is he neutered, microchipped?

Microchipped, I believe. Not a hundred percent. He's got a white patch on his chest, kind of shaped like, I don't know, Florida. And one ear is a little darker than the other. And he's friendly. He'll come up to anybody, so it's not like you'd have to be scared of him.
That's helpful. Friendly, white patch on the chest, darker left ear or right?
Hang on. Left. No wait, she told me, the left. Yeah, left.

Left ear. All right. I'll note that you're calling on behalf of the owner, and that she'd like a call back from the animal control officer. Is there a good time to reach you, since you're the contact?
I'm home most of the day. If I don't pick up, it's just the reception. Try twice. Or leave a message and I'll go stand in the bathroom and call back.

Will do. Also, if the owner wants to call us herself, she can, and we'll add her to the report. And if the poster is on city poles, that's generally fine for something like this, but I'd tell her to take them down once he's found.
Oh, yeah, she will. She's good about that. Okay, so that's it? It's registered?
It's logged as a lost dog report and I'm sending it over to animal control today. Someone should reach out to you.
Great. Thank you. That's all I needed.
You're welcome, Mr. Ricci. I hope Biscuit turns up soon.
Thanks. Bye.
